issues.detail: Error handling is limited to the missing-port case; failed builds, failed Blueprint syncs, rollbacks, and API error responses (rate limits, 401/404) are not covered.
Both examples are prose descriptions with no complete runnable YAML or command output, and Example 1 only lists fields to include instead of showing the full render.yaml.

scenarios.name: blueprint-secrets-and-db-wiring
scenarios.rationale: Both use fromDatabase with connectionString, fromService with type keyvalue, generateValue and sync:false, but A gives the keyvalue service `ipAllowList: []` while omitting it from the database, whereas B includes ipAllowList on both the keyvalue service and the database, with region consistency and a validate command, making B slightly more complete against the rubric.

scenarios.name: fix-no-open-port-deploy
scenarios.rationale: Both explain the 0.0.0.0:$PORT bind (default 10000) and use `render deploys create <id>`; A also recommends healthCheckPath and mentions the PORT=8000 alternative, while B omits healthCheckPath and the PORT=8000 option and adds extra material (a PATCH payload it admits it is unsure of).

scenarios.name: autoscaling-and-cron-modernized-config
scenarios.rationale: B covers all rubric items (scaling block, Pro workspace requirement, cron with UTC note, autoDeployTrigger, keyvalue) while A omits the Pro workspace note (it says Standard plan instead) but otherwise covers the rest; B is more complete on the rubric.
